name: Field_SpawnObjectRecordA
signature: void Field_SpawnObjectRecordA(FieldObject* self, uint32_t* rec, uint32_t arg3)
summary: First of three placement-record layouts: copies position/rotation words rec[0..5] and scale rec[7] into the field object, resolves the NPC talk-balloon entry, builds the sprite child descriptor (with the 'defaultTalk' string) and creates the model plus the actor sprite. The layout starts the transform at rec[0] (the other variants start at rec[4]/rec[8]).
evidence: New context: it is reached from the field scene spawn path (Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable -> Field_SceneObject_InitFromRecord chain) together with its siblings 0x00183C90 and 0x00184168, and its body is unambiguous about the role - rec words become f_2f8..f_30c/f_9c..f_a4, then maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC and maybe_Field_Actor_CreateSprite build the object. 'A' stays an ordinal because the dispatch that picks the layout is in unrecovered code.

name: Field_SpawnObjectRecordC
signature: void Field_SpawnObjectRecordC(FieldObject* self, int* rec, uint32_t arg3)
summary: Third placement-record layout (transform at rec[8..13], colour/type at rec[0x15..0x17], quest flags at rec[0x1e]/0x56/0x57): same model/sprite/scale resolution as the A and B variants, plus two extra sprite children and the field actor sound. Called once per record by the scene object-table spawner.
evidence: New context: Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTable / ...FromTableB / ...Thumb all reference it, so this is the record-group C branch of the scene spawn table; the body writes the same f_2f8..f_30c transform block as Field_SpawnObjectRecordA/B and ends with maybe_Model_SetupObject + maybe_Field_Actor_CreateSprite + maybe_Field_CreateActorSound.

name: Field_SceneObject_InitStaticModelFromLayout
summary: Initialises a static, layout-driven field scene object: two sprite children from the layout's 0x28-byte descriptor blocks, an fCol animator, a mesh from layout word 0x18, and (when the object id exists in the bag/flag table) its width/height words from the data manager.
evidence: New context: its only caller is the interior block 0x0034A8B8 inside the field scene-object spawner, which the N_126 pass documented as 'allocates and initialises one StaticModelFromLayout object through 0x0044A63C'; the body's Gfx_AddFColAnimator + Gfx_CreateMeshObjectByParams(self, layout->f_18, ...) sequence matches that reading, and layout->f_18 == 0x2d0 is stored as a flag.

name: Field_ActorGimmick_InitFromRecord
signature: void Field_ActorGimmick_InitFromRecord(void* self, int* record, unsigned int mode)
summary: Gimmick (actor-backed field object) initialiser from a placement record: copies the transform/colour fields, resolves the talk-balloon entry, applies the two sprite children and the model, then registers the actor sprite and its sound.
evidence: New context: the body is the same record-layout initialiser shape as Field_SpawnObjectRecordB (shared transform offsets rec[8..13], same balloon lookup and the same 0x5D-colour special case) but ends with maybe_Model_SetupObject + maybe_Field_Actor_CreateSprite + maybe_Field_CreateActorSound, i.e. the gimmick record variant; Field_Gimmick_InitFromRecord (0x002BE0E4) is the sibling entry point that reaches this record handling.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescMesh2
summary: Descriptor-driven scene-part initialiser: applies the transform, adds the colour animator when the descriptor carries a colour block, creates the mesh from desc->f_11 and loads the effect pack 0x69C. The '2' is an ordinal - the descriptor layout differs from 0x00472FE4 only in a few byte offsets.
evidence: Still ambiguous: the only caller is the low-confidence spawner 0x0035A1D0 (maybe_Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeC, 0.30) which allocates a 0x2F4-byte object, and no vtable or named caller ties this variant to a distinct class; the mesh/effect-pack body is confirmed, the ordinal name is not.

name: Field_SpawnObjectRecordB
signature: void Field_SpawnObjectRecordB(FieldObject* self, int* rec, uint32_t arg3)
summary: Second placement-record layout (transform at rec[4..9], model/colour at rec[0xd..0x10]): copies the transform, creates the two text/sprite children and the model, then sets the animator/shadow set. Same record group as Field_SpawnObjectRecordA, shifted by four words.
evidence: New context: referenced from the same scene spawn path as its siblings (Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTable*), and its body is the same transform+AddChildC/AddChildD+maybe_Model_SetupObject sequence; the shift-by-4-words relation to 0x00183984 is visible in the field offsets (f_2f8 <- rec[4] instead of rec[0]).

name: maybe_Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonA
signature: void maybe_Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonA(FieldNpc* self, const NpcPlacement* p, const u32* color, u32 owner)
summary: NPC placement-record initialiser that takes an explicit colour word instead of deriving it: copies the transform from p[8..13], stores *color into the balloon colour field f_38c, forces the balloon flag f_35d = 1, builds the sprite children/model and registers the actor sprite.
evidence: The body is confirmed (transform copy, self->f_38c = *color, f_35d = 1, AddChildC/AddChildD, maybe_Model_SetupObject) but 'Balloon' is still only inferred from the neighbouring Field_Npc_HasBalloonEntry / Field_FindNpcBalloonEntry calls and the shared f_35d flag; no caller or vtable slot names the NPC balloon object, so the specific wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonB
signature: void maybe_Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonB(FieldNpc* self, const NpcPlacement* p, const u32* color, u32 owner)
summary: Variant of the NPC placement-record initialiser with an explicit colour word: same transform/model/sprite sequence as 0x002FA83C with a different record offset base and colour mode, used where the caller already resolved the colour.
evidence: Body confirmed as the explicit-colour NPC record initialiser, but the 'B' ordinal and the 'Balloon' wording remain unproven - it shares no named caller or vtable with 0x002FA83C that would say which NPC kind selects it.

name: Effect_SphereEmitter_Setup
summary: Builds a spherical effect part from its definition: transform, colour, a radial fCol animator only when the radius vector def[3..5] is non-zero, then the mesh from def->f_c and the optional row-count reset on the emitter's list window.
evidence: New context: the named spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectSphereEmitter references it as its per-kind initialiser, and the body's non-zero radius test around the fCol animator is exactly the sphere-specific step (the sibling effect setups build the same animator unconditionally).

name: Effect_MeshEmitter_SetupE
summary: Mesh-effect part initialiser (variant E of the 0x44E6xx-0x44F7xx family): transform, colour, mesh from the definition's id and byte flags. The letter is an ordinal over the identical-shaped siblings.
evidence: New context: the named spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectMeshEmitterE calls it, so the 'mesh emitter' reading and the E slot come from the spawn dispatch rather than from the body alone; the body itself only differs from siblings in descriptor offsets.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescSmall
summary: Descriptor-driven billboard initialiser: selects the sprite mode from desc byte 0x3E (mode 3/4 also builds the quad child), applies a two-value scale/alpha set chosen by f_2C9 and creates the mesh. 'Small' only records the smaller of the two constant sets (2.5/0.75 vs 3.75/1.5); the class name is not proven.
evidence: Still ambiguous: its only caller is the low-confidence type-C spawner 0x0035A1D0 (0.30) that also calls 0x00471ABC, and the two differ only in f_2C9 and the scale/length constants, so 'Small'/'Large' describe measured constants, not a verified sprite size class.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescLarge
summary: Same descriptor-driven billboard initialiser as 0x004718A4 with f_2C9 = 1 and the larger scale/length constants (3.75/1.5/4.5 instead of 2.5/0.75/4.0). 'Large' is the measured constant difference, not a proven size class.
evidence: Still ambiguous: same single low-confidence caller (0x0035A1D0) as its sibling, and the only difference is the f_2C9 flag plus three float constants.

name: Field_SceneObject_BuildFromDesc
summary: Builds a field scene object from a descriptor block: transform and scale, one sprite child, the fCol animator and the mesh; called from the scene spawn block that handles 'object from descriptor' records.
evidence: New context: the named spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_ObjectFromDesc calls it (and Field_SceneObject_BuildFromDescAlt for the sibling variant), which fixes both the subsystem and the 'build from descriptor' role; the body's AddChildC + Gfx_AddFColAnimator + Gfx_CreateMeshObjectByParams chain matches.

name: Field_SceneObject_BuildFromDescAlt
summary: Alternate descriptor-driven field scene-object builder: same part-creation sequence as 0x004CAD68 with a different descriptor offset base, selected by the 'ObjectFromDescAlt' spawn block.
evidence: New context: the named spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_ObjectFromDescAlt references it, and the body repeats the transform/child/animator/mesh sequence of 0x004CAD68 with shifted offsets. 'Alt' is honest about being the second layout.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescAligned
summary: Descriptor-driven sprite-part initialiser for the 'aligned' spawn block: transform, optional colour animator, sprite child and mesh from the descriptor's aligned words.
evidence: New context: the named spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_SpriteActorAligned calls it, so 'Aligned' is the spawn-table slot name rather than a body-derived claim; the body is the standard maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC + Gfx_CreateMeshObjectByParams part builder.

name: Effect_UpdateBillboardOrientation
summary: Per-frame billboard orienter: runs the object's stored callback, resolves its owner node, builds a camera-facing basis from the billboard angles with std_Sinf/std_Cosf, uploads it to the device matrix at +0x7D4..+0x7FC and applies the resulting Euler rotation to the render node.
evidence: New context: the callees are now named (std_Sinf/std_Cosf, Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation) and the body's only side effects are the device-matrix write and the node rotation, which is exactly billboard orientation; no caller naming a different purpose exists.

name: Effect_HelixEmitter_Setup
summary: Builds a helical effect part from its definition: transform and colour, the fCol animator for the helix radius, then the mesh from the definition's id and flags.
evidence: New context: the spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectHelixEmitter references it as the per-kind initialiser, and the body differs from the sphere variant exactly in the animator setup, which is what makes the helix/sphere split meaningful.

name: maybe_Effect_MeshEmitter_SetupD
summary: Mesh-effect part initialiser of the 0x44E6xx family: transform, colour and mesh creation from the definition's id and byte flags; the letter is an ordinal over identical-shaped siblings.
evidence: Unlike its siblings D has no named spawn-block caller (no reference outside its own file), so the 'mesh emitter' reading rests on the shared body shape alone and the letter D cannot be tied to a spawn slot.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescVector
summary: Sprite/effect part initialiser that derives a direction vector from two descriptor points (normalised when longer than epsilon), stores it as the actor's motion/axis data at +0x2D4..+0x2E0, then applies transform, colour child and mesh.
evidence: New context: the spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_SpriteActorDescVector calls it, matching the vector-derivation body, so both the role and the 'vector' label are supported from the dispatch side.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescMesh
summary: Effect part initialiser that renders a single mesh/texture id: colour, position and rotation from the descriptor, a transform block from the inline template, one sprite child, then Gfx_CreateMeshObjectByParams and a clear of the animator's f_114/f_154 row counts.
evidence: The mesh half is certain (single Gfx_CreateMeshObjectByParams call with the descriptor's u16 id), but no named spawn block or caller references this address, so which spawn slot it serves is unknown.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescReleaseNodes
summary: Effect part initialiser that first releases the previously created model nodes (maybe_Gfx_ReleaseModelNodes) and then builds the new quad, its texture set and the fCol animator.

name: Gfx_ModelPart_InitSimple
summary: Model-part initialiser for plain coloured parts: copies the part fields, handles the 0x0FFFFFFF colour sentinel by reading the relative colour pointer, sets the position block and calls the sprite-child factory with the shared scale; no mesh is created.

name: Effect_BillboardEmitter_Setup
summary: Configures a single billboard (descriptor type 1) effect part: layer byte, the two sub-ids and the colour, one non-rotated sprite child whose scale is the definition's radius times the shared basis vector, and the colour mirrored into +0x2C8..+0x2D0.
evidence: New context: the spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectBillboardEmitter calls it, and the body builds exactly one child with descriptor type 1 - the same type byte the other effect setups use for the billboard path.

name: Effect_SelectEmitterVariant_Setup
summary: Configures an emitter whose particle comes from one of four variant groups: one sprite child with the definition colour/scale, then tests def[1]/def[3]/def[5]/def[7] in turn (first >= 1 wins), stores the chosen group (0..3) in f_2C8 and the referenced byte in f_2CC.
evidence: New context: the spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectSelectEmitter calls it, and the four-way selection loop with the 0xFF/-1 'none' defaults is visible in the body.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_InitMinimal
signature: void Gfx_SpriteActor_InitMinimal(SpriteActor* self, const SpriteDesc* desc)
summary: Smallest effect-part initialiser: only the transform, the colour child descriptor and the sprite child - no mesh, texture or animator call at all.
evidence: New context: the spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_SpriteActorMinimal calls it, and the body's only calls are Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation, the colour-desc builder and maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC, so 'minimal' describes it exactly.

name: Gfx_Node_SetFromEulerTransform
signature: u32 Gfx_Node_SetFromEulerTransform(u32 node, u32 parent, TransformEuler* transform)
summary: Applies a transform given as three Euler angles plus an offset: converts the angles with the shared sincos helpers, composes the 3x3 matrix and position, passes the world position to func_003D9A00 and the local offset to Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation; returns 1.
evidence: New context: the rotation helper is now named (Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation) and the body's sincos + matrix composition is visible; no caller names the function, so 'from Euler transform' is a description of the arguments rather than a documented API name.

name: maybe_Ui_List_BuildRowRecord
signature: void maybe_Ui_List_BuildRowRecord(u8* out, const u8* id, u32 mode, u32 flag)
summary: Builds one 0x84-byte 'name + count + icon' row record: resolves the row's name through the game tables, looks it up in the three-entry override table, measures the name with the text-width helpers, picks a count via Item_PickRandomByCategory and copies the record to out. Used both by the party status panel and by field HUD draw-object setup, so the record layout (not the caller) is what 'list row' refers to.
evidence: The callees are now named (Item_PickRandomByCategory, maybe_Pack_FindTableEntry, std_wcsncpy) and confirm the row-record build, but the callers are all still low confidence (maybe_Ui_PartyStatusPanel_Build 0.30, maybe_Field_Gimmick3107_SetupDrawObjectFromDesc 0.40), so neither the owning widget nor the exact row purpose is proven.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_MeasureAndLayoutText
summary: Wraps and lays out the text of a message window: copies the pending 0xFF-terminated run, walks the glyph id array accumulating the fixed-point line width at f_40C, inserts the line break/escape pairs (codes 1 and 4) when the width exceeds 1.0 and returns 1 when at least one line was produced. Also advances the reveal counter f_41C so the typewriter effect can continue.
evidence: New context: its two callers are now the named Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateOpen (0.55 - it feeds the wrapped buffer to Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextFromBuffer) and the dual-message-window update, so this is definitely the message-window wrap/measure step; the body's width accumulator and code 1/4 handling match the documented message-window line rules.

name: maybe_Ui_EffectHandleList_ReleaseAll
summary: Releases every instance in a UI 2D-effect handle list: walks the count at +0x18, validates each packed handle (index in the low 11 bits, generation above) against the global handle table, resolves the object and destroys it.
evidence: Correction of the subsystem: its only callers are Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateOpen (0.55) and Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateScrollText (0.55), not field effect managers, so the list belongs to the message window/UI, not to the field. The handle-table walk itself (0x007B80C0 + (handle & 0x7FF)*8, generation compare) is confirmed, but the object type behind 0x005F5818/0x005F5D24 is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_EffectHandleList_EnableAll
summary: Mirror of the release function: resolves every handle in the same UI effect list, calls the 'show/on' entry point on the object and finally sets the list's enabled flag at +0x1C.
evidence: Same correction as 0x0018F374 - the callers are the message-window open/scroll updates, so this is a UI effect handle list; the per-handle call 0x005F79C4(obj, 1) and the trailing f_1C = 1 are confirmed, but the object class behind the handle is not.

name: maybe_Ui_TalkLightWindow_Update
summary: Per-frame update of a talk/light overlay window: forwards a float parameter to the object's vtable slot +0x2C, runs the message-window update at +0x184, updates the 2D effect manager at +0xE50 and, when the flag at +0xE64 is set and the effect object at +0xEA0 is active, advances that effect's state.
evidence: The callees are now named (Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateOpen at +0x184, 0x0018FCF0 = 2D effect update) but no caller or vtable registration names the owning window, so 'TalkLightWindow' remains a guess from the first pass; the update role itself is confirmed.

name: Party_Member_ApplyPageContent
signature: void Party_Member_ApplyPageContent(void* self, const void* src, int mode)
summary: Applies one page of a party member record: resets the page glyph/width tables, copies the layout block and typing state from src, runs the text layout pass, and then reconciles the member's 24 inventory slots at +0xEC against the static id table 0x00190F10 - matching slots are removed (or un-equipped through 0x00191470) and re-marked 0xFFFF.
evidence: Corrected: the body is not pure text code - it is called by Party_Member_ApplyInventoryRecord (0.55) and by the two Text_Page builders, and after the layout pass it walks the member inventory (24 u16 at +0xEC, the FACTS.md member-inventory block), tests each slot with func_006292A4 (the six-byte equipped-slot list at +0x11C) and clears/un-equips matches, so it is item/equipment code on the member page.

name: Ui_EquipmentList_UpdateLayout
summary: Refreshes the equipment screen's two lists after a cursor/selection change: scrolls the member list by the pending delta, picks the f_654 or f_5f4 pane depending on which party slot the cursor is on, recomputes the row from f_F2C, and scrolls the chosen list to the clamped row.
evidence: New context: the body now reads as a chain of named equipment-list helpers - Ui_List_ScrollByDeltaRows12, maybe_Ui_ListCursor_IsAtPartyCountSlot / ...Plus1 / ...IsPastPartyCountSlots, Ui_EquipmentList_GetClampedRow, Ui_ScrollList_ScrollToIndex - which pins both the subsystem and the 'recompute row + scroll' role.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemDetail_Setup
summary: Fills the detail pane of an action/item window: sets message argument 5 from the selected entry (self->f_3570->f_51C), then argument 6 from a snapshot of party member 0 (func_0035EB98) - name, stats and the 0x200-byte status block - and finally switches the detail pane on.
evidence: The body is now readable in terms of named helpers (Message_SetArg, func_0035EB98 = party member record, Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim) and it is clearly a 'fill detail labels from the selected entry + party member' routine, but the owning window is only inferred from the f_3570 action-window pointer, so 'ItemDetail' stays a guess.

name: Ui_StatusWindow_SetOpen

name: Ui_MainWindow_ShowPane

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_SetVisibleAndSetTextLayers

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_SetVisible

The owning class ('ShopWindow') still rests only on the first-pass vtable association.

name: maybe_Ui_JewelShopWindow_SetVisible

name: maybe_Ui_SkillPanel_SetVisible

name: maybe_Ui_RecordListWindow_SetVisible

name: maybe_Ui_MessageSelectWindow_SetVisible

The old name collided with the real Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim at 0x001A6460.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_SetVisibleAndSetRowAlphas

Why each row state maps to which alpha is still unknown, and no named caller exists.

name: Ui_GridWindow_SetVisible
